analyst_view.overall: Early view: Inter Club d'Escaldes (35th, no points) have lost to Mjällby, Craiova and Red Star, the last one 2-1, and Domi Berlanga was sent off in that game, a UEFA match, so his ban applies here. Copenhagen (6th, seven points) are second in Denmark with 28 goals in 13 games and have beaten Braga 3-0 and Iberia 2-1. Copenhagen are clear favourites on a small ground in Encamp.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 1.9 for Copenhagen. Inter have conceded two or three in each European game and scored in two of them, so a 2-1 or 3-1 Copenhagen win fits the number well; I stay with it.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, split evenly. I would expect Copenhagen to win more of them than the even split suggests, but I have no evidence that moves the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Inter finished their last game with Berlanga sent off and a home side chasing the ball for long spells tends to foul, but the number already sits fairly high and no referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.4 shots, almost evenly split. I would expect Copenhagen to take more than 12.4 and Inter fewer than 11.1, but the total looks reasonable, so I stay with it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Copenhagen's attack is in form domestically; with Inter conceding regularly, the number looks about right.
